EXAMPLE 04 · Hard · max/examples/custom_ops/fused_attention.py

Attention, one key tile at a time.

See why a larger running maximum requires rescaling the previous output.

O = softmax(Q Kᵀ) V · unscaled, rank 2

Follow Bazel → target code ↓Follow the operationRead original Python + Mojo

Tiny view: one query, four keys, two features; original CPU N=D=8 / GPU N=D=32. Follow Bazel build actions into MAX's runtime MLIR graph compiler, Mojo specialization and target-specific code; then follow one connected operation and three focused graph/compiler/kernel zooms. Section 00 has build/run commands. SOURCE follows this repository's pinned code. IR sheets, numeric tiles and device motion illustrate the mechanism; they are not compiler dumps or measured MAX/GPU execution.

Set up, build and run this exact example

SOURCE · repository build rule / locked Pixi environment

The steps show the repository-root Bazel build and generated example-test, plus the separate Pixi setup and task for running the Python script directly.

Bazel · build, then run the test

Run from the repository root, the directory containing bazelw. The wrapper bootstraps its pinned Bazelisk when needed. The test target is generated by custom_op_example_py_binary; it runs the binary and fails if the process exits non-zero. Numerical assertions come from the Python example. The preceding build is optional because bazelw test builds its dependencies.

./bazelw build //max/examples/custom_ops:fused_attention
./bazelw test //max/examples/custom_ops:fused_attention.example-test

The generated Bazel test carries the gpu tag. The Python examples select CPU when no accelerator is detected; otherwise they request an accelerator.

Pixi · set up the environment, then run the script

Install the Pixi CLI first. Run setup once in the example directory; pixi install resolves the declared Python/MAX dependencies from the project environment and lockfile.

cd max/examples/custom_ops
pixi install
pixi run fused_attention

pixi run fused_attention invokes python fused_attention.py, as declared in pixi.toml. This route runs the example script directly; it does not invoke the Bazel test wrapper.

This Bazel test is marked manual and disabled in CI in this checkout. Naming its target directly runs the requested test.

    MAX OpState._CAPIPtr exports the existing operation in an MLIR capsule · Operation capsule creation and named-pointer extraction · PyOperation::createFromCapsule: extract, validate, obtain context, wrap
    Portable pointer handoff
    1. Export _CAPIPtr as a Python capsule → CAP1: named PyCapsule, pointer=P. MAX calls wrap(getOperation()), then PyCapsule_New. No IR data is serialized; the capsule has no keep-alive destructor.
    2. Extract and check the C API handle → MlirOperation { ptr=P }. PyCapsule_GetPointer checks the expected operation capsule name. The valid path retains P; a wrong name raises.
    3. Create the MLIR Python wrapper → G1._mlir_op → PyOperation → OP1. The factory obtains OP1’s context and creates a PyOperation wrapper. OP1 remains attached to MODULE1.
    4. Read the existing region and body → _current_block = _graph_body = B0. regions[0].blocks[0] retrieves B0. No GraphOp, region or block is cloned or created by this lookup.
    _CAPICreate(op._CAPIPtr) creates another wrapper around the SAME native GraphOp. CAPI means the MLIR C API used between MAX's nanobind wrapper and MLIR's Python bindings. There is no graph clone or serialized IR here.

  → _CAPIPtr: named PyCapsule(pointer=P)
  → MlirOperation {ptr=P}
  → MLIR Python PyOperation(pointer=P, context reference)
  → existing region R0 / block B0

    Python records one opaque attention call; it does not run softmax or translate arbitrary Python into Mojo. The insertion helper unwraps operands, converts result types, inserts the operation in G1's body, and creates symbolic result wrappers.
    

    // Schematic MO: full printed dialect syntax may differ
module {
  mo.graph @fused_attention(%q:T, %k:T, %v:T) -> T {
    %ch = mo.chain.create()
    %o = mo.custom(%q,%k,%v) {
      symbol = "modular_ops::fused_attention_custom",
      parameters = {BD=8:index, BN=16:index}, device=gpu:0
    } : (T,T,T) -> T
    mo.output %o
  }
}
// T describes float32 [32,32] on gpu:0; no matrix data here.

    JIT means just-in-time compilation: code generation requested by the running MAX process. This example calls session.compile(graph) before supplying numeric buffers. The kernel code is prepared there (or reused from a cache), rather than running mojo build for every matrix execution.

    KGENCompiler runs elaboration. ObjectCompiler lowers and translates into LLVM IR. The compiler-side TargetBackendRegistry selects a registered backend by target triple; architecture/features configure target codegen.
    

    NVIDIA example: nvptx64-nvidia-cuda, illustrative arch sm_90a, NVPTX backend → PTX and device binary route. AMD example: amdgcn-amd-amdhsa, illustrative arch gfx942, AMDGPU backend → AMDGPU object/ELF route. The cross-target source test supplies both architecture examples.
    

    The host Python/MAX runtime and compiled host glue stay on CPU. Device kernels have separate offload targets. P1 .mojoc preparation is a distinct earlier subprocess. Architecture examples are not GPU detection or execution results.

    Why a CPU worker? Engine::Context::initModel schedules setup on the CPU runtime so the task has the correct AsyncRT CPUDevice association. Setup may depend on asynchronous resources; the caller waits for readiness instead of pretending initialization is already complete.

    Each key tile updates one stable max, denominator, and normalized output per query row. The source computes an unscaled, rank-2 softmax(QKᵀ)V: no heads, batch, mask, dropout, or 1/√D scale.
    

    m_new = max(m_old, max(S_tile))
alpha = exp(m_old - m_new)
E = exp(S_tile - m_new)
l_new = alpha*l_old + sum(E)
O_new = O_old * alpha*l_old/l_new + (E/l_new) @ V_tile

    

    Why rescale? When a later maximum grows, earlier exponentials were measured against an older maximum. Multiplying their retained mass by alpha expresses them relative to the new maximum. Multiplying old normalized O by alpha*l_old/l_new also adjusts for the new denominator.

    Source initializes m with the dtype's minimum value; the teaching model uses mathematical −∞ for readability. See max, denominator, and output update/store.

            Keep the example in view.
            This example is unscaled rank-2 attention without mask/dropout/heads. GPU BN=16, BD=8 but its key tile BN_1=8. CPU BN=4, BD=4. The original script prints output Buffers and has no explicit CPU copy or parity assertion. The tiny online-softmax comparison is independently checked in JavaScript.
            What the scenes prove and illustrate
            • SOURCE: repository example, shapes, registration strings, parameters, compiler architecture, target backend and runtime APIs. Revision 610f7111836d9a950d45ba52ec9b3e0ed589fe3f.
            • ILLUSTRATION: small fixed inputs, representation sheets and binary labels, optimized/unfused comparison, tile occupancy, queues and hardware motion. Backend support and actual lowering depend on the installed toolchain and target.
            • BOUNDARY: native device scheduling, transfers and execution timing. No MAX model compilation, inference or GPU measurement is claimed.
            • These scripts call compile and init separately, passing runtime tensors to execute. Prepared MEF bytes are distinct from initialized M1; no MEF export or model weights registry appears in these scripts.
            • CPU fallback avoids a fictitious GPU transfer or GPU block barrier. Numerical illustrations use JavaScript arithmetic; they do not validate MAX kernel parity.

23def main() -> None:
24    mojo_kernels = Path(__file__).parent / "kernels"
25
26    dtype = DType.float32
27
28    # Place the graph on a GPU, if available. Fall back to CPU if not.
29    device = CPU() if accelerator_count() == 0 else Accelerator()
30    if accelerator_count() == 0:
31        N = 8
32        D = 8
33        BD = 4
34        BN = 4
35    else:
36        N = 32
37        D = 32
38        BD = 8
39        BN = 16
40
41    with Graph(
42        "fused_attention",
43        input_types=[
44            TensorType(
45                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
46            ),
47            TensorType(
48                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
49            ),
50            TensorType(
51                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
52            ),
53        ],
54        custom_extensions=[mojo_kernels],
55    ) as graph:
56        q, k, v, *_ = graph.inputs
57        results = ops.custom(
58            name="modular_ops::fused_attention_custom",
59            device=DeviceRef.from_device(device),
60            parameters={"BD": BD, "BN": BN},
61            values=[q, k, v],
62            out_types=[
63                TensorType(
64                    dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
65                )
66            ],
67        )
68        graph.output(*results)
69
70    # Set up an inference session for running the graph.
71    session = InferenceSession(devices=[device])
72
73    # Compile the graph.
74    compiled = session.compile(graph)
75    model = session.init(compiled)
76
77    np.random.seed(123)
78    Q = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
79    K = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
80    V = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
81
82    output = model.execute(Q, K, V)
83    print(output)
84
85
86if __name__ == "__main__":
87    main()

14"""
15The code below computes the attention score for a tile of size BN x BD.
16It follows the exact arithmetic as described in the FlashAttention-2 paper
17(https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08691). The variable names in this program
18reflect the variable names in the algorithms from the paper.
19
20Here, the following tensors are Q for the query,
21K for the key, V for the value, and O for the output.
22
23       Q            K               V
24  +----D----+  +----D----+   +--+--BD--+---+
25  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
26  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
27  +---------+  |.........|   |  |......|   |
28  |.........|  |.........|   |  |......|   |
29  BN........|  N.........|   N  |......|   |
30  |.........|  |.........|   |  |......|   |
31  +---------+  |.........|   |  |......|   |
32  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
33  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
34  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
35  +---------+  +---------+   +--+------+---+
36
37The main trick is in the softmax computation.
38As the paper says, S and P are intermediate values.
39
40Let S = Q * K^T  ∈ R^{N, D}
41    P = Softmax(S) ∈ R^{N, D}
42The attention score is O = P * V ∈ R^{N, D}.
43
44One way to think about this is to consider what happens if we
45split the dimensions N in  K, and Q into two tiles: K_1 and K_2, V_1 and V_2.
46Then we can incrementally compute the output as follows:
47  S_1 = Q * K_1, S_2 = Q * K_2
48  O_i = O_{i-1} * renormalization_factor + softmax(S_i) * V_i
49
50This allows for the incremental computation of softmax(S_i) * V_i,
51leading to the final output.
52"""
53
54

57from max.gpu.sync import barrier
58from layout import TensorLayout, TileTensor, row_major, stack_allocation
59from layout.math import max, sum
60from layout.tensor_core import TensorCore
61

63
64from std.utils import Index

67@register("modular_ops::fused_attention_custom")
68struct FusedAttention:
69    """Registers the `fused_attention_custom` op, allowing python to use it from the `max`
70    package.
71    """
72
73    @staticmethod
74    def execute[
75        dtype: DType,
76        rank: Int,
77        //,  # Forces the previous two params to be inferred from the args
78        BN: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split Q into
79        BD: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split K, V into
80        target: StaticString,  # "cpu" or "gpu"
81    ](
82        output: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
83        query: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
84        key: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
85        value: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
86        ctx: DeviceContext,
87    ) raises:
88        comptime assert rank == 2, "rank must be 2"
89
90        # Query tensor
91        var Q = query.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
92        # Key tensor
93        var K = key.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
94        # Value tensor
95        var V = value.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
96        # Attention output tensor
97        var O = output.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
98
99        comptime if target == "cpu":
100            print("Running on CPU")
101            fused_attention_cpu[BN, BD](Q, K, V, O)
102        else:
103            var dev_ctx = ctx
104            print("Running on GPU")
105            fused_attention_gpu[BN, BD](dev_ctx, Q, K, V, O)

132@inline(.always)
133def matmul_b_transpose(
134    lhs: TileTensor,
135    rhs: TileTensor,
136    out res: TileTensor[
137        lhs.dtype,
138        type_of(row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()),
139        MutUntrackedOrigin,
140    ],
141):
142    res = stack_allocation[lhs.dtype](
143        row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()
144    )
145
146    comptime for m in range(lhs.static_shape[0]):
147        comptime for n in range(rhs.static_shape[0]):
148            res[m, n] = 0.0
149
150            comptime for k in range(lhs.static_shape[1]):
151                res[m, n] += rebind[res.ElementType](
152                    lhs[m, k].cast[res.dtype]()
153                ) * rebind[res.ElementType](rhs[n, k].cast[res.dtype]())
154
155
156# The bulk of the code below implements what the papers calls
157# an "online softmax", which is local to each block.
158# The algorithm is described as:
159#
160# $$$
161# m_1 = rowmax(S_1)
162# l_1 = rowsum(e^(S_1-m_1))
163# P_1 = diag(l_1)^-1 * e^(S_1-m_1)
164# O_1 = P_1*V_1 = diag(l_1)^-1 * e^(S_1-m_1) * V_1
165# m_2 = max(m_1, rowmax(S_2)) = m
166# l_2 = e^(m_1-m_2) * l_1 _ rowsum(e^(S_2-m_2))
167#     = rowsum(e^(S_1-m)) + rowsum(e^(S_2-m)) = ls
168# P_2 = diag(l_2)^-1 * e^(S_2-m_2)
169# O_2 = diag(l_1/l_2)^-1 * O_1 + (P_2 * V_2)
170#     = diag(l_2)^-1 * e^(S_2-m) * V
171# $$$
172
173
174@inline(.always)
175def fused_attention_cpu[
176    BN: Int, BD: Int
177](Q: TileTensor, K: TileTensor, V: TileTensor, O: TileTensor[mut=True, ...],):
178    comptime N = K.static_shape[0]
179    comptime D = K.static_shape[1]
180
181    comptime for tile_n in range(N // BN):
182        var Q_tile = Q.tile[BN, D](tile_n, 0)
183
184        comptime for tile_d in range(D // BD):
185            var m_1 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(
186                Scalar[Q.dtype].MIN
187            )
188
189            var l_1 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(0)
190
191            var O_i = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN, BD]()).fill(0)
192
193            comptime for tile_n_idx in range(N // BN):
194                var K_tile = K.tile[BN, D](tile_n_idx, 0)
195                var V_tile = V.tile[BN, BD](tile_n_idx, tile_d)
196
197                var S = matmul_b_transpose(Q_tile, K_tile)
198                var m_2 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
199                max[axis=1](S, m_2)
200                m_2.max(m_1)
201
202                # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
203                var l_2 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
204                l_2.copy_from(m_1)
205                l_2 -= m_2
206                l_2.exp()
207                l_2 *= l_1
208                var E = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN, BN]())
209                E.copy_from(S)
210                E -= m_2
211                E.exp()
212                var l_2_sum = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
213                sum[axis=1](E, l_2_sum)
214                l_2 += l_2_sum
215
216                # P = exp(S - m_2) / l_2
217                E /= l_2
218                O_i *= l_1
219                O_i /= l_2
220                var m_1_delta = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
221                m_1_delta.copy_from(m_1)
222                m_1_delta -= m_2
223                m_1_delta.exp()
224                O_i *= m_1_delta
225                var PV = matmul["cpu"](E, V_tile)
226                O_i += PV
227                m_1.copy_from(m_2)
228                l_1.copy_from(l_2)
229
230            O.tile[BN, BD](tile_n, tile_d).copy_from(O_i)
231
232
233@inline(.always)
234def matmul[
235    dtype: DType,
236    rhs_dtype: DType,
237    //,
238    target: StaticString,
239    transpose_b: Bool = False,
240](
241    lhs: TileTensor[dtype, ...],
242    rhs: TileTensor[rhs_dtype, ...],
243    out res: TileTensor[
244        dtype,
245        type_of(row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()),
246        MutUntrackedOrigin,
247        address_space=lhs.address_space,
248    ],
249):
250    res = stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=lhs.address_space](
251        row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()
252    )
253
254    comptime if target == "cpu":
255        comptime for m in range(lhs.static_shape[0]):
256            comptime for n in range(rhs.static_shape[1]):
257                res[m, n] = 0.0
258
259                comptime for k in range(lhs.static_shape[1]):
260                    res[m, n] += rebind[res.ElementType](
261                        lhs[m, k].cast[res.dtype]()
262                    ) * rebind[res.ElementType](rhs[k, n].cast[res.dtype]())
263    else:
264        comptime M = lhs.static_shape[0]
265        comptime N = rhs.static_shape[0]
266        comptime K = lhs.static_shape[1]
267
268        var out_sram = stack_allocation[res.dtype, address_space=.SHARED](
269            row_major[M, N]()
270        )
271
272        comptime BK = 8
273
274        comptime assert K % 8 == 0, "K needs to be a multiple of 8"
275
276        var mma_b_t = TensorCore[dtype, dtype, Index(M, N, BK), transpose_b]()
277
278        var c_reg = stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=.LOCAL](
279            mma_b_t.c_fragment_layout
280        ).fill(0)
281
282        # `TensorCore`'s native loads require matching operand dtypes;
283        # rebind the B view once when `rhs` carries a different dtype.
284        var rhs_typed = rebind[
285            TileTensor[
286                dtype,
287                rhs.LayoutType,
288                rhs.origin,
289                Engine=rhs.Engine,
290                address_space=rhs.address_space,
291                linear_idx_type=rhs.linear_idx_type,
292            ]
293        ](rhs)
294
295        comptime for k_i in range(K // BK):
296            var a_reg = mma_b_t.load_a(lhs.tile[M, BK](0, k_i))
297
298            var b_reg = mma_b_t.load_b(rhs_typed.tile[BK, N](k_i, 0))
299
300            comptime if transpose_b:
301                b_reg = rebind[type_of(b_reg)](
302                    mma_b_t.load_b(rhs_typed.tile[N, BK](0, k_i))
303                )
304
305            var d_reg = mma_b_t.mma_op(a_reg, b_reg, c_reg)
306            c_reg.copy_from(d_reg)
307        mma_b_t.store_d(out_sram, c_reg)
308
309        barrier()
310        res.copy_from(out_sram)
311
312
313def fused_attention_kernel[
314    q_dtype: DType,
315    q_layout: TensorLayout,
316    k_dtype: DType,
317    k_layout: TensorLayout,
318    v_dtype: DType,
319    v_layout: TensorLayout,
320    o_dtype: DType,
321    o_layout: TensorLayout,
322    BN: Int,
323    BD: Int,
324](
325    Q: TileTensor[q_dtype, q_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
326    K: TileTensor[k_dtype, k_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
327    V: TileTensor[v_dtype, v_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
328    O: TileTensor[o_dtype, o_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
329):
330    comptime N = Q.static_shape[0]
331    comptime D = Q.static_shape[1]
332
333    var Q_tile = Q.tile[BN, D](block_idx.y, 0)
334
335    var m_1 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(
336        Scalar[q_dtype].MIN
337    )
338    var l_1 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(0)
339    var O_i = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN, BD]()).fill(0)
340
341    comptime BN_1 = 8
342
343    for tile_n_idx in range(N // BN_1):
344        var K_tile = K.tile[BN_1, D](tile_n_idx, 0)
345        var V_tile = V.tile[BN_1, BD](tile_n_idx, block_idx.x)
346        var S = matmul["gpu", transpose_b=True](Q_tile, K_tile)
347        var m_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
348        max[axis=1](S, m_2)
349        m_2.max(m_1)
350
351        # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
352        var l_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
353        l_2.copy_from(m_1)
354        l_2 -= m_2
355        l_2.exp()
356        l_2 *= l_1
357        var E = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN, BN_1]())
358        E.copy_from(S)
359        E -= m_2
360        E.exp()
361        var l_2_sum = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
362        sum[axis=1](E, l_2_sum)
363        l_2 += l_2_sum
364
365        # P = exp(S - m_2) / l_2
366        E /= l_2
367        O_i *= l_1
368        O_i /= l_2
369        var m_1_delta = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
370        m_1_delta.copy_from(m_1)
371        m_1_delta -= m_2
372        m_1_delta.exp()
373        O_i *= m_1_delta
374        var PV = matmul["gpu"](E, V_tile)
375        O_i += PV
376        m_1.copy_from(m_2)
377        l_1.copy_from(l_2)
378    O.tile[BN, BD](block_idx.y, block_idx.x).copy_from(O_i)
379
380
381def fused_attention_gpu[
382    BN: Int,
383    BD: Int,
384](
385    ctx: DeviceContext,
386    Q: TileTensor,
387    K: TileTensor,
388    V: TileTensor,
389    O: TileTensor[mut=True, ...],
390) raises:
391    comptime kernel_func = fused_attention_kernel[
392        Q.dtype,
393        Q.LayoutType,
394        K.dtype,
395        K.LayoutType,
396        V.dtype,
397        V.LayoutType,
398        O.dtype,
399        O.LayoutType,
400        BN,
401        BD,
402    ]
403    ctx.enqueue_function[kernel_func](
404        Q,
405        K,
406        V,
407        O,
408        grid_dim=(Int(Q.dim[1]()) // BD, Int(Q.dim[0]()) // BN),
409        block_dim=(32),
410    )

331    comptime D = Q.static_shape[1]

349        m_2.max(m_1)
350
351        # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
352        var l_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
353        l_2.copy_from(m_1)
354        l_2 -= m_2

            494static void gcPipelineImpl(mlir::OpPassManager &pm,
495                           const GCPipelineOptions &opts, bool skipJit,
496                           bool dumpIntermediates) {
497
498  auto kernelLibraryPaths =
499      llvm::to_vector_of<std::string>(opts.kernelLibraryPaths);
500
501  // Filled by the first ("mo") dump from the non-subgraph model names while
502  // the GraphOps still exist; later dumps reuse it.
503  auto dumpBaseName = std::make_shared<std::string>();
504
505  if (dumpIntermediates)
506    pm.addPass(MO::createDumpStagePass("mo", dumpBaseName));

            Per-target triple, architecture and backend lookup [C++:L213]
            213/// Given the pre-elaboration function `func` belonging to a module with the
214/// symbol table `symtab`, slice out a standalone module rooted at `func`,
215/// elaborate it, and compile it for `target`.
216static ErrorOr<StringAttr> compileStandaloneKernel(
217    GeneratorOp func, SymbolConstantAttr symbol, StringAttr name,
218    const SymbolTable &symtab, TargetInfoAttr target, EmitAs emissionKind,
219    EmissionOptions emissionOptions, CompilationOptions compilationOptions,
220    ElaborateGeneratorsOptions elaboratorOptions) {
221  // Configure the compilation options given the new target.
222  compilationOptions.targetTriple = target.getTripleStr();
223  compilationOptions.targetCpu = target.getArch();
224  compilationOptions.targetFeatures = target.getFeatures();
225  compilationOptions.targetAbi = target.getAbi();
226  if (compilationOptions.targetAccelerator.empty()) {
227#if MLRT_ACCELERATOR_SUPPORT
228    compilationOptions.targetAccelerator =
229        Driver::Device::getAcceleratorArchOrEmpty();
230#endif
231  }
232  compilationOptions.relocModel = target.getRelocationModel();
233  StringRef targetDataLayout = target.getDataLayout().toString();
234  if (!targetDataLayout.empty())
235    compilationOptions.targetDataLayout = targetDataLayout;
236
237  // Pull `target-abi` out of the emission options and apply it directly to
238  // `compilationOptions` before the target machine is created: `createTarget-
239  // Machine` reads `targetABI` as a struct field, not by re-querying LLVM's
240  // registered `-target-abi` cl option, so letting it flow through the
241  // generic cl-parsed list below would only mutate global state unseen here.
242  compilationOptions.targetABI.clear();
243  applyTargetABIEmissionOptions(emissionOptions, compilationOptions.targetABI);
244  SmallVector<StringRef> clEmissionOptions;
245  llvm::copy_if(
246      emissionOptions, std::back_inserter(clEmissionOptions),
247      [](StringRef item) { return !isTargetABIEmissionOption(item); });
248
249  // Initialize the object compiler.
250  PassManagerConfigOptions pmOptions;
251  pmOptions.applyPassManagerCLOptions = true; // enable print options
252  ErrorOr<std::unique_ptr<ObjectCompiler>> compilerOr = ObjectCompiler::create(
253      kMojoCacheBaseDirName, compilationOptions, /*isJIT=*/
254      false, *target.getContext(), pmOptions);
255
256  if (compilerOr.isError())
257    return compilerOr.takeError();
258
259  std::unique_ptr<ObjectCompiler> compiler = compilerOr.takeValue();
260
261  // A backend that owns offload lowering drives its own lower+emit and needs
262  // no LLVM TargetMachine.
263  ErrorOr<const TargetBackend *> backendOr =
264      TargetBackendRegistry::get().lookup(target.getTriple());
265  const TargetBackend *backend = backendOr.isError() ? nullptr : *backendOr;
266  bool backendOwnsOffload = backend && backend->ownsOffloadLowering();
267
268  std::unique_ptr<llvm::TargetMachine> tm;
269  if (!backendOwnsOffload) {
270    ErrorOr<std::unique_ptr<llvm::TargetMachine>> tmOr =
271        createTargetMachine(compilationOptions, /*isJIT=*/false);
272    if (tmOr.isError())
273      return tmOr.takeError();
274    tm = tmOr.takeValue();
275  }

            TargetBackendRegistry resolves the LLVM triple · complete unchanged source
            TargetBackendRegistry resolves the LLVM triple [C++:L114]
            114void TargetBackendRegistry::add(std::unique_ptr<TargetBackend> backend) {
115  Backends.push_back(std::move(backend));
116}
117
118ErrorOr<const TargetBackend *>
119TargetBackendRegistry::lookup(const llvm::Triple &triple) const {
120  // A backend that resolves `triple` to one it owns takes precedence over a
121  // direct self-match.
122  const TargetBackend *result = [&]() -> const TargetBackend * {
123    const TargetBackend *directMatch = nullptr;
124    for (const std::unique_ptr<TargetBackend> &backend : Backends) {
125      const TargetBackend *resolved = backend->resolve(triple);
126      if (!resolved)
127        continue;
128      if (resolved != backend.get())
129        return resolved;
130      if (!directMatch)
131        directMatch = resolved;
132    }
133    return directMatch;
134  }();
135  if (!result) {
136    return Error("target '" + triple.str() +
137                 "' is not supported by this build");
138  }

            Documented Pixi setup and run path · complete unchanged source
            Documented Pixi setup and run path [DOC:L55]
            55A single [Pixi](https://pixi.sh/latest/) command runs each of the examples:
56
57```sh
58pixi run addition
59pixi run mandelbrot
60pixi run vector_addition
61pixi run top_k
62pixi run matrix_multiplication
63pixi run fused_attention
64pixi run image_pipeline
65```
66
67`pixi run <example>` runs the associated Python example, taking care
68to ensure the necessary dependencies (i.e. the `max` package) are visible.
69The Python code will construct the graph and related inference session state.
70The Mojo kernels code defining the custom operations will be (re)compiled on the
71fly as needed, ensuring the executing graph is always using the latest version
72of the Mojo code.
